thread:
matt: Heads up — merge check on PR #4125 failed: evidence fingerprint mismatch for artifact `build/signature.tar.gz`. The signer job tried to pull the key and KMS returned AccessDenied. Anyone owning the evidence/attachments flow able to triage?
julia: cc @aisha @raj — saw the same from the nightly job earlier. Wasn't sure if it was a short-lived grant. We need to know whether to fallback to the unsigned attachment path.
aisha: I'm on it. Quick Q: is this the repo-level signing keystore (keystore-prod) or the ephemeral CI key? logs show: `kms:AccessDenied` for key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/repo-signer`
raj: that key was rotated yesterday for rotation testing. We applied a conditional IAM binding that should allow `ci-service@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for 2h windows. Maybe windows expired.
matt: thanks. If the CI can't fetch the key, the current merge check rejects the PR because fingerprint != stored evidence. Is there an allowed fallback?
sec-bot: [automated] Merge check failed: artifact fingerprint mismatch (sha256). CI job id: `ci-2026-03-21-0912`. See /ci/logs/ci-2026-03-21-0912 for full trace.
aisha: we do have a fallback for transient KMS failures: we can mark the evidence as "pending-attestation" and allow a staged merge with a canary label, but that requires an explicit owner sign-off. Not automatic.
julia: we should avoid manual signoffs often. Could we instead have the runner use an alternate signing key that lives in dedicated keystore (keystore-aux) with stricter audit but broader permissions? That would let merges continue while keystore team fixes rotation.
raj: aux key is possible but needs an audit trail: who used it, why. Also we'd want a TTL and automated backfill to sign artifacts once primary key is available.
matt: Implementation suggestion: when KMS AccessDenied, CI should: 1) set PR label `attestation:pending`, 2) attach unsigned evidence blob and a short note with failure reason, 3) notify owners channel and block auto-merge. Then keystore team runs a backfill job that re-signs artifacts and re-runs the fingerprint check. Thoughts?
aisha: +1. Also add an assert in the backfill that ensures key used for re-signing is the original key or database records the re-signing key id. We need clear provenance.
someone (matt): pseudo-command for backfill we discussed:```bash
# re-sign artifact
gcloud kms keys versions list --key ring=ci --key=repo-signer
gcloud kms encrypt --key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/repo-signer \
  --plaintext-file=build/signature.tar.gz --ciphertext-file=build/signature.tar.gz.enc
# update PR evidence metadata
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"pr":4125, "evidence_status":"signed", "signer_key":"projects/.../repo-signer/versions/42"}' \
  https://api.redwood.internal/evidence/update
```
raj: that looks fine. We should also add a small audit script that records KMS response codes into evidence metadata: `kms_response=AccessDenied` etc.
julia: operationally, who gets paged if this happens again during business hours vs off-hours? We need an oncall routing.
aisha: sec-oncall handles evidence-related keystore issues M-F 9-5. Outside that, `infra-oncall` owns CI runner credentials. Add both to the notification runbook via escalation: sec-oncall -> infra-oncall -> keystore-team.
ci-bot: @channel PR #4125 merge check: attestation pending. Labels added: `attestation:pending`. Notifying: @sec-oncall, @infra-oncall.
matt: perfect. I'll add a short PR comment template that explains steps and points to the backfill ticket template. Also opening a short runbook PR to codify fallback logic, labels, and backfill process.
aisha: assign to me and raj for the runbook PR. I'll also add the required audit fields: original_fingerprint, attempted_key, kms_status, re_sign_key, re_sign_time.
raj: I'll stake the CI-side changes (labeling + evidence payload). aisha can own the backfill + audit schema.
matt: thanks — please ping here when the PRs are up and when we enable the temporary aux-key policy, so I can un-block the PR. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: [automated] Incident note created: `INC-2026-03-21-KMS-AccessDenied-PR4125`. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-03-21-KMS-AccessDenied-PR4125
julia: re: long term, let's add a periodic smoke check that exercises the signer key and alerts if the conditional grant is about to expire. Could be a weekly cron.
aisha: agreed. I'll add that to the runbook too.
matt: closing loop — filing the runbook PR now. Will follow up with links.
